Subject: DeltaEdge — post-call technical recap & deployment matrix

Hi Sara / Carlos — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your engineering and procurement teams have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Top-level pain & goals (your priority ordering):
- Latency-sensitive inference for interactive product features (95th pctile < 120ms for short prompts, target worst-case tail < 250ms).
- High QPS during peak windows (burst to ~1,200 qps with steady-state ~300 qps).
- Data residency in US-East; some regulated customer segments require VPC/private deployment.
- Cost target: ~35% reduction vs current self-hosted baseline using batching + quantized variants.

Technical constraints we captured:
- Primary model family: open Llama-2-70B (quantized MQA/8-bit) for ranking + summarization workflows; smaller 13B variant for low-latency product paths.
- Typical input lengths: 40-120 tokens; longform summarize path up to 2k tokens (rare).
- KV cache reuse expected across related user sessions (session affinity important).

Proposed topology options (short):
1) Hosted + Dedicated burst: Redwood hosted endpoint for baseline and canary; Dedicated pool in US-East for sustained throughput and VPC peering for regulated traffic.
2) Private (VPC) single-tenant install: recommended for regulated segments — customer-managed infra, Redwood control plane with KMS integration.

SLO mapping (draft):
- Interactive (primary): 95th <= 120ms; P99 <= 350ms; availability 99.9%
- Background/summarize: median <= 800ms; P95 <= 2s
- Throughput: sustain 300 qps; burstable to 1,200 qps for up to 10 minutes with graceful degraded routing into 13B fallback if capacity constrained.

Next steps (owner / due):
- Jonas: update MAP and send version w/ pricing shades for Hosted vs Dedicated (EOD Thu). [Attachment: deltaedge-mutual-action-plan.xlsx]
- DeltaEdge (Sara/Carlos): confirm which customer segments require VPC-only and provide compliance checklist (by Mon).
- Rishi / Marissa: draft deployment topology sketch with estimated GPU counts (Rishi: perf model; Marissa: ops/runbook) (first draft Wed).

Attachments I’m including: initial MAP, SLO matrix, rough topology sketch.

Thanks — pleased with alignment.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jonas_weber@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: deltaedge-mutual-action-plan.xlsx]

Jonas — thanks for the thorough write-up, this aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications from product/eng: 

- The 95th < 120ms requirement is for our customer-facing search box (single-turn). The summarize longform path can tolerate higher latency and we can batch.
- For bursts: the 1,200 qps figure is an upper bound — more likely we see 800–1,000 qps sustained for ~5–8 minutes during promotions.
- We do require VPC for healthcare-tier customers; other segments can be hosted. Will confirm the compliance checklist by Monday.

Quick ask for the topology sketch: can you call out expected VM/GPU types per model variant (70B quant vs 13B) and an ops fallback flow for degraded QoS? Our infra team wants to see concrete numbers to model cost.

Carlos and @engineering, feel free to add specifics.

Thanks,
Sara Park
VP Product | DeltaEdge

Sara / team — quick engineering follow-up from Redwood infra perspective. I’ve annotated three concrete items we’ll include in the topology sketch and cost model: 

1) Perf baselines and GPU sizing:
   - Llama-2-70B (MQA/8-bit): expect ~45–60ms/token on A100-80GB equivalent with optimized kernels; ~9 tokens/s per stream for batched long requests. For interactive short prompts (avg 60 tokens) we recommend 4x A100-80GB equivalents per 1,000 qps with batching windows tuned to 8–12ms to preserve tail latency.
   - Llama-2-13B: single-stream latency ~12–18ms for typical short prompts on T4-like or A10 equivalents; good candidate for low-latency fallbacks.

2) KV cache & session affinity:
   - We'll sketch a sticky routing layer to preserve KV cache hit rates for repeat session requests; recommend Redis-backed prefix cache for cross-instance cold-start reduction.

3) Degraded flow and graceful fallback:
   - Primary: 70B quantized variant for quality-critical routes.
   - Fallback path: when dedicated pool saturation occurs, route to 13B low-latency variant + admit-rate limiting for background summarization. Include auto-scaler thresholds and fallthrough timers.

I’ll produce a simple capacity table (GPUs, estimated QPS per instance, steady vs burst) and attach it to the topology sketch. Jonas — will need the MAP to align cost buckets.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-latency-throughput-matrix.pdf]
